answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a stake-backed reputation trellis: each identity locks a deposit and earns trust only through completed, peer-attested jobs, so reputation cannot be bought instantly. A new fake starts with zero history and low limits, and must spend real time and money doing honest work before taking large jobs. Fraud is punished by slashing the deposit and burning that history, like a dropped marble shattering glass. The loss then ripples to linked identities sharing the same stake or fingerprints, raising the cost of many fakes above any gain from one scam.
